verdict.rationale: Proa ships its own first-party full-stack layer on top of its core rendering crate. `proa new site` scaffolds an Axum-backed app [proa-docs-2, proa-docs-28], and a separate proa_framework_core crate handles serving [proa-gh-8]. Routing is documented through `src/routes.rs` registration, `proa site routes` and route-level page caching [proa-docs-10, proa-docs-11, proa-docs-12]. Data fetching is covered by loader caching and request-scoped data via WebContext, plus Suspense streaming for slow data [proa-docs-18, proa-docs-35]. missing for 10: in-depth docs on the data-loader API (only a one-line mention of loader caching), an explicit description of the meta-framework/core layering, independent or hands-on corroboration.
